items.body:
Sainsbury’s deploys RFID technology for Tu clothing range across 400 of UK grocery retailer’s stores
Sainsbury's is rolling out radio frequency identification (RFID) technology across its TU clothing departments in approximately 400 stores, with the project set for completion by early September.
This follows a pilot earlier this year, which enabled the retailer to improve its stock level visibility, speed up replenishment and manage stock more efficiently.
“Really proud of my team and the role they’ve played in deploying this project across our stores. A huge amount of work, collaboration and energy behind the scenes to bring this to life,” says Gillian Ekin, Head of Transformation and Operational Development at Sainsbury’s.
RTIH has reached out to Sainsbury’s regarding specifics of the implementation, such as suppliers involved, and we will update this article when we receive a response.
The wrong lens
Until people start viewing RFID through the correct lens, they’ll keep massively underestimating what the technology actually unlocks. So says Dan McGrath, JD Group Customer Operations, JD Sports.
In a LinkedIn post, McGrath, a member of the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards judging panel, said: "I hate RFID. Not because it doesn’t work. Not because it isn’t valuable. But because most of the industry is still looking at it through the wrong lens"
He added that RFID has never been about stock accuracy for him. Rather, it’s about stock confidence. "Accuracy is a report. Confidence is a decision. And in an agentic world where everything is about speed, automation, and autonomous decision-making, confidence is the only thing that actually matters."
"Because what’s the point in being 98% accurate, if an agent can’t trust that last 2%? In an age of velocity: Can I confidently sell this item? Can I confidently promise it to a customer? Can I confidently route demand to this store? If the answer isn’t 100% yes, the system breaks."
McGrath continued: "That’s the shift people are missing. RFID isn’t a store ops tool anymore. It’s a confidence engine for agentic commerce. And this is exactly why we chose Checkpoint Systems and ItemOptix. Because it’s a fully serviceable, API first RFID platform.”
“That means I can use RFID as a live data layer, connecting the physical store to autonomous systems, agents, and whatever comes next. Stores stop being places with stock and start becoming real-time, queryable inventory nodes. That’s the game. The industry is still talking about cycle counts."
He concluded: "The reality? We’re building infrastructure for machines to trade physical goods. And until people start viewing RFID through that lens, they’ll keep massively underestimating what it actually unlocks."
2026 RTIH Innovation Awards
RFID technology will be a key focus area at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards.
The awards are now open for entries and celebrate global retail technology innovation in a fast moving omnichannel world.
Our winners will be revealed at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Ceremony, taking place at The HAC in Central London on Wednesday, 4th November.
Check out our 2025 winners here.
Our 2025 hall of fame entrants were revealed during a sold out event which took place at The HAC on 16th October and consisted of a drinks reception, three course meal, and awards ceremony presided over by award winning comedian, actress and writer Tiff Stevenson.
In his welcome speech, Scott Thompson, Founder and Editor, RTIH, said: “This is the awards’ fifth year as a physical event. We started off with just 30 people at the South Place Hotel not far from here, then moved to London Bridge Hotel, then The Barbican, and last year RIBA’s HQ in the West End.”
“But I’m conscious of the fact that, to quote the legend that is Taylor Swift, You’re only as hot as your last hit, baby. So, this year we’ve moved to our biggest venue yet, and also pulled in our largest number of entries to date and broken attendance records.”
He added: “This year’s submissions have without doubt been our best yet. To quote one of the judges: The examples of innovative developments across both traditional and digital retail spaces were truly remarkable.”
Congratulations to our winners, and a big thank you to our sponsors, judging panel, the legend that is Tiff Stevenson, and all those who attended our 2025 gathering.

items.body:
Lefties lands in UK and Walmart rethinks payments strategy: last week’s biggest retail technology plays
RTIH rounds up the stand out retail technology deals, launches, deployments and pilots from the past seven days. Including Dollar General, RELEX Solutions, M&S, Officeworks, Zitcha, Tesco, Simbe, Toolstation, Kroger, Uber Eats, Nkuku, Sweetwater, and Dickey's Barbecue Pit.
M&S
M&S says it has become the first retailer to use AI powered monitoring systems on its entire Milk Pool to monitor animal welfare across 46 dairy farms. The tools use cameras to capture footage of dairy cows when they are indoors which is then analysed using an algorithm trained alongside vets to monitor welfare of dairy cows in real-time.
The technology uses AI powered video analytics to build an individual health profile for each animal, tracking mobility and body condition scoring over time to give farmers objective, consistent data on the wellbeing of their herd. The tools monitor the cow’s behaviour including lying time, feeding time, social interactions and mobility to generate a ‘cow comfort score’ which supports vets in their assessment of individual cow’s health. The cameras will assess body condition scoring to assess cows’ nutritional status over time.
Terry Canning, CEO of Cattle Eye says “Changes in body condition are early indicators of metabolic health, fertility, and overall wellbeing. Tracking those changes more regularly, across every cow, gives farmers a level of insight that was previously unavailable outside research environments.”
The algorithm supporting the tool has been tested and, according to those involved, found to perform to the same standard as a trained welfare assessor.
The tools are being rolled out following trials at a selection of M&S dairy farms, where farmers have used the technology to make changes to tailor care to individual cow’s needs. By measuring lying times, farmers have made changes to the bedding of individual cows to improve their comfort based on their specific size and shape. Feeding schedules have been adapted to reduce the amount of time cows spend standing and the design of some stalls has been adapted to improve cow comfort.
Lefties
Landsec reports that the first Lefties store in the UK has opened its doors at Liverpool ONE. Owned by Inditex, the fashion retailer has launched a flagship store on South John Street, spanning over 27,000 sq ft across two floors, stocking women’s, men’s, teen, kids, baby, newborn, home, accessories and footwear collections.
This will feature some of the brand’s latest retail technology, already introduced at recent European openings, including robotic hanger sorters and radio frequency identification self-checkouts, removing the need to scan each item separately.
Pablo Sueiras, Head of Retail & Hospitality Leasing at Landsec, says: “Lefties making its UK debut at Liverpool ONE is a significant milestone for the destination and highlights its continued appeal to retailers looking to establish themselves in the UK market. Lefties’ arrival builds on our long standing relationship with Inditex and the success of its existing brands at Liverpool ONE. It also reflects the confidence global retailers have in the destination’s ability to deliver the scale, visibility and highly engaged customer base needed to support long-term growth.”
With the addition of the UK, Lefties is now present in 20 markets globally with 225 stores.
Toolstation
Edenred Payment Solutions (EPS) reports the launch of a new closed loop gift card programme for Toolstation, a UK omnichannel retailer of tools, accessories and building supplies. This enables DIY enthusiasts and trade professionals to purchase and redeem gift cards across all Toolstation touchpoints, including in-store across its network of over 550 UK branches, online, or through the retailer’s mobile app.
Powered by EPS’s API-based payments platform, the programme provides Toolstation with end-to-end card processing capabilities, including real-time top-ups, balance enquiries, and secure redemptions built directly into its checkout systems with zero third-party redirects. EPS also equips the Toolstation team with dedicated customer service management tools and analytics dashboards to monitor activity, breakage, customer behaviour, and campaign performance.
Rehana Mitha, Managing Director at Edenred Payment Solutions, says: "Toolstation is the latest retailer to recognise the importance of incorporating gift cards into their customer proposition. They wanted to create a brand new programme with zero friction when their customers were using the gift card, regardless of how they choose to purchase and redeem across stores, the web and app.”
“They set an ambitious goal of integration, card manufacture, and launch in their stores in just eight weeks. Our dedicated project team worked with great agility and close collaboration with several Toolstation stakeholders to meet this timeline. We are thrilled to support Toolstation with an end-to-end payment solution that promotes long-term customer loyalty while also giving rise to meaningful community and B2B initiatives in the future."
Dollar General
RELEX Solutions is partnering with Dollar General to implement forecasting, replenishment, and allocation capabilities across its North American operations.
Dollar General operates more than 21,000 stores and 34 distribution centres, managing approximately 18,000 SKUs, and continues to expand its store footprint each year. The AI driven RELEX platform will manage store replenishment, ordering schedules, lead times, supplier coordination, and fulfillment methods in one place. Sales patterns and other demand factors will be built directly into the planning process, allowing DCs and stores to work from the same data.
“We chose RELEX because it gives us a practical way to use AI in our planning and helps our teams focus on the issues that truly need attention,” says Jeff Vaughan, SVP Global Inventory Management at Dollar General. “The platform brings forecasting, replenishment, and allocation planning into a single environment, giving our teams greater visibility across the network.”
Sweetwater
Sweetwater, an online retailer for music makers, has chosen Gr4vy, a cloud-based payment orchestration platform, as it looks to modernise its payment infrastructure and simplify operations through a single orchestration layer.
“This partnership reflects what payment orchestration is all about: giving merchants the freedom to evolve their payment strategy without rebuilding their infrastructure,” says John Lunn, Founder and CEO at Gr4vy. “Our role is to provide payment infrastructure that gives businesses like Sweetwater the flexibility to adapt as they grow.”
“Gr4vy gives us the flexibility to simplify our payment infrastructure while making it easier to evolve our payment strategy over time,” says David Stineburg, Director of Payments and Fraud Prevention at Sweetwater. “The implementation was collaborative from day one, and we're excited to continue expanding our partnership.”
Officeworks
Australian retailer Officeworks, part of the Wesfarmers group, has become the first retailer globally to activate Snapchat's suite of advertising formats directly within the Zitcha platform. This includes Sponsored Snaps, Snapchat's in-chat ad format that delivers full screen video or images directly into the Chat feed; Snap Ads (single image or video) to drive awareness, engagement, traffic and sales; and catalogue powered Dynamic Product Ads to blend storytelling with dynamic product discovery.
Officework kicked things off with a campaign for Microsoft to drive demand both online and in-store.
Andy Mossop, Chief Customer Officer at Officeworks, says: “We're focused on building a retail media network that creates value for everyone in the ecosystem, our customers, our suppliers and our business. That's why we're incredibly proud to partner with Zitcha and Snapchat to bring this innovative integration to life. As one of the first retailers globally to activate Snapchat through Zitcha, we're helping shape the future of retail media by connecting brands with audiences in more relevant and engaging ways.”
“Just as importantly, we're committed to delivering meaningful, measurable results for our suppliers. This work is a great example of what's possible when retailers, technology partners and brands come together with a shared focus on customer relevance and impact. We’re proud to provide a platform that delivers on this breadth of benefit to our supplier partners.”
Petsense by Tractor Supply
A new partnership makes Instacart the exclusive same-day delivery partner for Petsense by Tractor Supply. Customers can now shop Petsense's assortment of pet foods and supplies through the Instacart app and website, with delivery in as fast as an hour with no markups.
"Petsense has built a loyal following among pet owners who care deeply about the wellbeing of their animals," says Blake Wallace, Vice President of Commercial Partnerships at Instacart. "We're thrilled to be its exclusive same-day delivery partner, making it easier than ever for customers to get the specialty products their pets love, whenever they need them."
"We believe that ensuring the health and happiness of your pets should be the easiest decision you make in a day," says Shawn Blankenship, Vice President of Petsense by Tractor Supply, which has over 130 stores across the US. "By partnering with Instacart to offer same-day delivery, customers can now receive our top-quality assortment of pet food and supplies in as little as an hour. This partnership represents our commitment to being the most convenient and dependable place to shop for your pets."
Post Office
OneView Commerce has signed a contract with the Post Office to deliver a new electronic point of sale (EPoS) system across all its branches.
The deal is valued at £141 million. It is part of the Post Office's wider programme to replace its legacy Horizon system and modernise technology across its branch network, a central pillar of its five-year transformation plan.
OneView will work alongside the Post Office and Accenture, which is separately leading the transition of day-to-day Horizon operations and back end development, to deliver the new EPoS platform.
Kroger
Grocery and prescription delivery is now available across nearly all Kroger banners in the US, including Fred Meyer, Ralphs and Harris Teeter. The Instacart powered capability connects customers to more than 2,200 Kroger pharmacy locations.
Eligible prescriptions are filled and verified by Kroger pharmacy teams before being delivered from the store by an Instacart shopper.
"We're committed to making it easier for our customers to take care of their health and their families," says Colleen Lindholz, President at Kroger Health. "This new service combines the convenience of grocery delivery with the personalised care provided by our pharmacy teams. Customers have groceries and eligible prescriptions delivered together, knowing their prescriptions are filled and verified by the trusted Kroger pharmacy teams who serve their communities every day."
"Grocery delivery has always been about removing friction from people's lives, and picking up a prescription is one of the most important errands customers manage," says Ryan Hamburger, Chief Commercial Officer at Instacart. "Together with Kroger, we're making it easier for customers to access groceries and pharmacy services in one order, bringing greater convenience to everyday life while preserving the trusted pharmacy experience customers depend on."
Uber Eats
Uber Eats is bringing robot delivery to the EU. This week, Finland will become the first EU market where its customers can get their orders delivered by autonomous robots, starting in central Helsinki through a partnership with Coco Robotics. Customers matched with a robot can follow its journey in the Uber Eats app.
A spokesperson says: “We’re growing fast in Finland. We launched Uber Eats in May with three cities, and just three months later we’re adding eight more, bringing us to 11 cities and areas across the country. Helsinki is a particularly exciting place to take this next step: the robots have already been put through their paces on the city’s streets and in Finnish winter conditions. Now they’ll be delivering for Uber Eats alongside our existing courier network.”
SPAR
ZetaDisplay has extended its partnership with SPAR to deliver the retailer’s first retail media network. This follows ZetaDisplay’s recent acquisition of retailmediatools, a retail media infrastructure-as-a-service platform.
The roll-out for SPAR has begun with a pilot programme and will continue through to the end of the year. ZetaDisplay’s Austria team, which has collaborated with SPAR for more than a decade, will lead the project. Over the years, the partnership has delivered a series of in-store digital solutions, including the evolution of dining experiences through dynamic digital menu boards, deli counter screens, kiosk ordering systems, mosaic walls as well as employee information screens.
The deployment will see the installation of hundreds of new displays, establishing a digital signage network that supports both retail media and broader in-store communications. The project also includes the repositioning of current displays to better align with evolving shopper behaviours, leveraging ZetaDisplay’s ongoing research into customer journeys and in-store engagement.
The entire network will be powered by ZetaDisplay’s proprietary Engage Suite, which will also be implemented across SPAR’s Slovenian stores. Engage Suite enables content creation, scheduling and management, while providing analytics and measurement tools to deliver the right message to the right audience at the right time. SPAR will retain full control over its retail media ecosystem, including the ability to approve which brands can advertise across its network, while also leveraging the platform to promote its own campaigns.
Walmart
Walmart is adding tap to pay options to its checkout stations at US stores and Sam's Club warehouses, with deployment set for completion by end of year. Fuel stations will be upgraded by mid-2027. This includes options like Apple Pay and Google Pay.
Walmart has long resisted the rise and rise of NFC-based payments, opting instead to go all in on its Walmart Pay app and Scan and Go app features for contactless payments.
In a LinkedIn post, Sam Amrani, Founder and CEO at PassBy, said: "Isn't it crazy to think that it's 2026 and Walmart doesn't accept Apple Pay? Until now that is. This has been a case of America's largest retailer vs America's largest consumer tech company."
He added: "Inevitably, Walmart Pay will go down as the largest attempt at creating a closed loop payment system. Its demise will be the final nail in the coffin for retailers trying to create proprietary payment rails for their ecosystem. Ultimately, convenience wins."
"The consumer is the kingmaker, and the result was clear, the convenience of Apple Pay was too important to the customer journey. It will make customers happier and Walmart - although adopting reluctantly - will see this lead to faster transaction times, happier customers and more visits."
Tesco
Last month we reported that Tesco was trialling Simbe’s Tally in-store shelf scanning robot.
Having kicked off with a single store, the pilot is now being extended to a small number of other locations. Thanks to Toby Pickard, Retail Futures Senior Partner at IGD, and a member of the judging panel for the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards, for bringing this to our attention.
In a LinkedIn post, he said: “I’ve now seen Simbe’s Tally robot in a third Tesco store in the UK - another store trialling autonomous inventory scanning. But this time, I had my son with me. His reaction was fascinating. He was completely intrigued by Tally: watching it move around the store, trying to work out what it was doing, and following it with the kind of curiosity only a child can bring to something that feels like it has just stepped out of the future.”
He added: “I’ve heard that in the US, some shoppers will even choose stores specifically because they have Tally, because their children love seeing the robot. Honestly, I can believe it. And it got me thinking…We often talk about retail automation in terms of efficiency, accuracy, labour productivity and ROI. But what happens when the technology itself becomes part of the customer experience? Could robots like Tally become something that customers - and especially children - actively want to see?”
Could, Pickard asked, the presence of robots change which stores people choose to visit? And perhaps more importantly: what happens when the next generation grows up thinking autonomous robots moving around a supermarket is completely normal? Will they see Tally as technology? Or simply as part of what a modern store is?
Pickard concluded: “There’s a fascinating intersection here between automation, operations, customer experience and the psychology of physical retail. I’m increasingly convinced that the question isn’t just, what can robots do for retailers? It’s also, what can robots make customers feel about the future of retail?”
Nkuku
Back.tech is partnering with Nkuku to improve how it manages consumer returns, reverse logistics and recommerce.
In a LinkedIn post, Giorgio Vitale, Co-founder and CRO at Back.Tech, said: "A big part of what makes this special is Operations & Impact Director Chris Wilson’s vision for reverse logistics at Nkuku - moving beyond current state returns processing to a smarter, connected reverse lifecycle for every product."
"This means rethinking returns across the full operation: DTC e-commerce - streamlined parcel returns; Big and bulky items - smarter grading, routing and resale decisions; B2B supplier returns - improved visibility and control upstream to optimise downstream requirements; Recommerce - maximising value through quicker resale and redistribution. This is exactly where we add new value."
Back.tech's AI powered grading and dynamic routing engine helps businesses accurately assess condition, automate decisioning, and optimise where every item should go next.
For Nkuku, this will improve reverse logistics performance by: Reducing operating costs through automation and fewer manual decisions; Improving delivery and handling efficiency across return flows; Unlocking net savings by routing items to the highest value recovery path faster and more accurately; Increasing recovery rates across both parcel and bulky inventory streams.
California Pizza Kitchen
California Pizza Kitchen is set to roll-out up to 1,000 automated pizza making kiosks across the US through a partnership with T-ROC Global. The pair will target real estate with high foot traffic, like hospitals, hotels, campuses, and sports venues, where opening a full sized restaurant would be impractical.
The offering will use TurboChef powered cooking, touchscreen technology and data driven systems. According to California Pizza Kitchen, the kiosks can prepare a pizza in as little as 90 seconds. The menu is expected to extend beyond pizza. Plans are afoot to offer items including Kung Pao and Bolognese spaghetti, Mac ‘N’ Cheese varieties and the brand’s Butter Cake.
California Pizza Kitchen began testing automated retail in 2025. Machines are now operating at airports including Boston Logan International Airport, Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport, Dallas Love Field and Dayton International Airport. The company also expects to activate another 15 at universities by the end of 2026.
“For decades, CPK has been dedicated to meeting consumers wherever they are, whether through our global restaurant network, airport and non-traditional locations, off-site events, or the local grocery store where we’ve been a leading premium pizza brand for 25 years,” says Michael Beacham, President at California Pizza Kitchen Global. “Our automated retail strategy, now accelerated through a partnership with T-ROC, introduces CPK to entirely new occasions and venues where consumers desire quality food on the go.”
Dickey's Barbecue Pit
Dickey's Barbecue Pit has announced the launch of three new interactive mobile games exclusively for Big Yellow Cup Rewards members. Memory, Big Yellow Cup Flip Challenge and Catcher, a custom development feature by Spark Adriatic, are the first games out of the game as part of this loyalty roll-out.
Customers can earn loyalty points while playing them within the Dickey's mobile app. The move is a reaction to nearly 30% of all online orders now being placed through the company's mobile app.
Laura Rea Dickey, CEO, says: "We're always looking for new ways to make every barbecue experience more rewarding. Our Big Yellow Cup Rewards members are some of our most loyal guests, and these new mobile games give them another fun reason to open the app, engage with our brand and earn rewards they can use toward their next barbecue meal."

The Home Depot has bagged the Holy Grail of omnichannel retail with its latest AI shopping assistant move
The Home Depot has announced the US wide roll-out of new in-store capabilities for Magic Apron, its Al powered shopping assistant. Customers can open it in the retailer’smobile app or scan a QR code on in-store signage.
"Customers come to The Home Depot for expert guidance, and we know they want their shopping experience to be easy and efficient," says Jordan Broggi, EVP of Interconnected Retail. "Magic Apron takes the best of our digital expertise and brings it into the physical store, creating a more connected shopping experience that helps customers find products, get project guidance and make decisions faster. Our associates remain at the centre of the shopping experience, and Magic Apron gives customers another way to access guidance and support while they're in our stores."
This is the Holy Grail of omnichannel retail, according to Michael Guzzetta, Retail Innovation & Strategy Leader at Cookie Plug San Antonio, and a former H-E-B executive.
In a LinkedIn post, he said: “It's moments like these when an AI assistant stops being just another digital feature and starts making physical promises a reality. Customers can ask questions by text, voice, or image. Then, Magic Apron can provide project guidance, check local availability, and even point someone to a specific aisle and bay. The model is the visible part for the customer, but the harder job will be for the back end teams to keep several operating systems honest at the same time: Local inventory; Aisle and bay mapping; Product compatibility; Store specific knowledge; The handoff to an associate when the answer is incomplete or wrong.”
He added: “Anyone who has worked around store systems knows that “aisle 14, bay 6” isn’t just a helpful customer answer... It’s a promise built on receiving, stocking, planogram changes, shrink, inventory accuracy, and whatever happened on the floor ten minutes ago. Now zoom out to a nationwide scale and the important questions change. How quickly does local reality reach the assistant? How does an associate correct a bad answer? Who owns the recovery when the guidance is technically sound but the product isn’t actually there?”
Magic Apron is compelling because it connects advice to the physical store, Guzzetta argues. Its biggest test will be how often the store can keep the promise its digital friend just made.

items.body:
Walmart takes Subway restaurant delivery offer beyond store estate following summer launch
In June we reported that Walmart, in a move that saw it locking horns with DoorDash and Uber Eats, was enabling customers in select locations to order Subway directly through the US retail giant’s app or Walmart.com and have their meal delivered in as little as 30 minutes or less, either on its own or alongside their Walmart Express Delivery order.
This marked Walmart’s first restaurant integration within Express Delivery as it looks to bring groceries, household essentials, fashion, prescriptions and restaurant meals together in one experience. And it has now gone a step further.
"When we launched restaurant delivery with Subway earlier this summer, we had a simple idea: make it easier for customers to get a meal alongside the groceries and everyday items they turn to Walmart for," says Greg Cathey, SVP, Digital Fulfilment Transformation.
"After four months of successful deliveries, we are taking the next step by expanding restaurant delivery beyond Subway restaurants located inside Walmart stores. That means customers can increasingly turn to Walmart for meals from locations both inside and outside our stores, while still having the option to combine that meal with their Walmart order."
"Since launch, nearly 65% of restaurant orders were delivered along with items from Walmart the customer needed quickly. That could be sandwiches for dinner with groceries for tomorrow morning, or lunch alongside a few household essentials. We’ve created a new kind of shopping occasion for customers that brings together a meal and the things they need from Walmart in one delivery."
He adds: "We are learning a lot about how customers are using the new service, including the fact that restaurant delivery is introducing more customers to Express Delivery. One of the things I find most interesting is what happens after that first restaurant order. One in five orders that has both Subway and Walmart items is a customer’s first time using Express Delivery this year, and nearly 30% of those customers come back within 30 days."
"That is a strong indicator that once customers experience the convenience of Express Delivery, they find more reasons to use it for other moments in their lives. There is a lot more ahead, but these first few months are a great example of what happens when we bring together the things customers already count on Walmart for: convenience, value, selection and increasingly, speed."
"Thank you to the Walmart and Subway teams who have helped bring this experience to life. Twenty years into our relationship, it is exciting to keep finding new ways to serve customers together."

European consumer electronics chain Mediamarkt Saturn opens Tech Village in Cologne, Germany
Mediamarkt Saturn has opened its tenth Tech Village, with the latest one being located in Cologne, Germany. In a LinkedIn post, Guido Monferrini, EVP and Regional CEO, said: “In 2020, we opened the very first Tech Village in Milan. This week marked an exciting new milestone: Tech Village Cologne is officially open!”
He added: “As our 10th Tech Village in Europe, it is built on years of experience, learnings and continuous innovation. One of our greatest challenges was to refresh and redefine the concept, transforming it into a modern, inspiring environment that reflects our future vision and serves as the blueprint for future European Tech Villages.”
“At its core, it is all about experience: we want to offer everyone the opportunity to discover and engage with the most cutting-edge, immersive technology. By combining inspirational experiences with personal consultation and seamless service, we build what matters most: lasting trust with our customers.”
Key features: A redesigned in-house store concept with a tech driven layout, large format digital media surfaces, and an atmospheric lighting design; Immersive 3D experiences bringing products and technology to life alongside 31 brand boutiques; Integrated Xperion: Bringing a 1,000+ sqm gaming destination and 200-seat arena under the same roof.
Monferrini concluded: “Bringing a vision of this scale to life is a demanding and complex undertaking. The successful realisation of this project is the result of the dedication, expertise, creativity and teamwork demonstrated throughout every phase of the journey. A heartfelt thank you to my concept and construction team and to the German team for their fantastic collaboration on this remarkable achievement.”

items.title: Shein shapes up for cut-price IPO as dominance slows
items.summary: Shein will list in Hong Kong this week in a cut-price initial public offering following two previous failed attempts in London and New York. The Chinese retailer will begin trading in Hong Kong on Tuesday in a debut set to value the firm at around $27bn (£19.8bn), about a quarter of its highest private-market valuation. [...]
items.body:
Shein shapes up for cut-price IPO as dominance slows
Shein will list in Hong Kong this week in a cut-price initial public offering following two previous failed attempts in London and New York.
The Chinese retailer will begin trading in Hong Kong on Tuesday in a debut set to value the firm at around $27bn (£19.8bn), about a quarter of its highest private-market valuation.
Shein will offer nearly 280m shares at between HK$47.60 and HK$49.50, expecting to raise about HK$13.6bn.
The online retailer has surged in popularity in recent years, putting pressure on household high street names like Zara and H&M with its combination of rock-bottom prices and super-fast delivery.
While this public market debut should be a moment of triumph for the fast-fashion seller, the price and location of this offering marks a significant downfall for the firm.
Shein had first sought a listing in the US in 2023, but ditched the plans following pushback from the Securities and Exchange Commission. Lawmakers had raised concerns over alleged labour malpractices and lawsuits from the retailer’s US competitors.
The Singapore-headquartered firm then turned to London, where it filed for a £50bn float. Shein faced pressure from MPs over a “lack of candid and open answers” to allegations that its supply chain was linked to forced labour and human rights abuses.
Tax crackdown threatens sales
The retailer’s filing for a public float in Hong Kong was initially seen as a power play designed to pressure the UK’s Financial Conduct Authority into approving its London listing.
But Shein has now pressed ahead with its cut-price Hong Kong float as it faces growing balance sheet and regulatory pressures.
“Appropriately enough for a business which made its name selling clothes at discount prices, Shein looks set for a cut-price IPO,” AJ Bell investment director Russ Mould said.
The firm swung to a $99m loss in the first three months of this year, compared to a net income of $395m in the year before.
“[But] Shein still has strengths as a retail business, which include identifying and latching on to emerging trends at pace, significant flexibility in its supply chain and a large global customer base,” Mould added.
One of the drags on Shein’s once-buoyant sales is the emerging crackdown on a tax loophole which had been a huge boon to the e-commerce giant and its rivals, like Chinese-owned Temu.
Shein said last month that the US’s decision to scrap a rule which had exempted small packages from import duty had hit its sales in the key market.
“In response to the increased duties and taxes, we are pursuing a wide range of options, including increasing our prices in the US market to offset a portion of the increased costs,” the group said in its accounts.
This tax loophole, known as the ‘de-minimis’ threshold, was closed in the EU earlier this month and the UK government is set to introduce its crackdown on the rule in October 2028.
Fast fashion declines in popularity
But British high street retailers, including Primark and Accessorize, have urged the government to bring forward this measure, which has already been accelerated by six months, meaning that Shein could see its UK sales put under threat even sooner.
“That could gradually narrow the price gap between Shein and high-street rivals such as Primark and H&M, taking some of the sparkle out of its ultra-cheap offering,” said Wealth Club’s chief investment strategist, Susannah Streeter.
Shein is also coming to terms with a fashion market that is much changed from the insatiable appetite for fast fashion which rocketed the company to dominance a few years ago.
Second-hand platforms like Vinted and Ebay have seen a resurgence in popularity as consumers turn to retro styles and more sustainable shopping practices.
“Fast fashion is far less popular than it was a decade ago, with the rise of resale websites proving tough competition, given that shoppers can get their hands on higher-end brands, at a fraction of the price, to refresh wardrobes,” Streeter said.
Shein was co-founded in 2008 by Chinese entrepreneur Chris Xu, also known as Xu Yangtian. The retailer’s IPO is being led by Wall Street heavyweights JP Morgan, Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley.

items.body:
Everseen, Hanshow and Vusion are so hot right now: last week's most read retail systems articles
Check out our most clicked retail technology articles from last week, including Starship Technologies, White Castle, Murphy USA, M&S, Uber Eats, Coco Robotics, Tesco, Simbe, and the first ever RTIH Retail Technology Hot 100 List.
Everseen, Hanshow and OpenAI top first ever RTIH Retail Technology Hot 100 List
In partnership with 3D Cloud, RTIH is pleased to launch its first ever Retail Technology Hot 100 List. We’re bringing you the hottest companies whose solutions and systems are helping drive the retail sector forward.
These companies operate across the omnichannel retail landscape (stores, online, mobile, supply chain, payments etc).
Our judging panel, including Vineta Bajaj, Group CFO, Holland & Barrett, Dan McGrath, JD Group Customer Operations, JD Sports, Dr. Astha Purohit, Director of Product Management, Customer Data and Identity, Walmart, and Paula Bobbett, Chief Data and Digital Officer, Boots, provided feedback on those who have the most innovative, forward thinking technology offerings and are also best addressing retailers' current challenges, painpoints, and opportunities.
The judges used the following framework when making their picks:
1. Retailer problem fit - how meaningful, strategic, and widely felt the retailer pain being addressed is.
2. Production traction in retail (2025–2026) - real named retailer deployments, pilots. 
3. Innovation and defensibility - genuine technical novelty paired with a defensible competitive position. 
And there was also a public vote, with thousands of members of our community of retail tech enthusiasts getting involved. Thanks to all those who took part! Based on the judging panel's feedback and the public vote, we then drew up our first ever RTIH Retail Technology Hot 100.
So, without further ado, here are the 100 hottest global retail technology ventures right now. Drum roll, please…
You can download the hot 100 in pdf format here. Enjoy!
Tesco extends its UK trial of Simbe's in-store autonomous inventory scanning solution Tally
Last month we reported that Tesco was trialling Simbe’s Tally in-store shelf scanning robot.
Having kicked off with a single store, the pilot is now being extended to a small number of other locations. Thanks to Toby Pickard, Retail Futures Senior Partner at IGD, and a member of the judging panel for the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards, for bringing this to our attention.
In a LinkedIn post, he said: “I’ve now seen Simbe’s Tally robot in a third Tesco store in the UK - another store trialling autonomous inventory scanning. But this time, I had my son with me. His reaction was fascinating. He was completely intrigued by Tally: watching it move around the store, trying to work out what it was doing, and following it with the kind of curiosity only a child can bring to something that feels like it has just stepped out of the future.”
He added: “I’ve heard that in the US, some shoppers will even choose stores specifically because they have Tally, because their children love seeing the robot. Honestly, I can believe it. And it got me thinking…We often talk about retail automation in terms of efficiency, accuracy, labour productivity and ROI. But what happens when the technology itself becomes part of the customer experience? Could robots like Tally become something that customers - and especially children - actively want to see?”
Could, Pickard asked, the presence of robots change which stores people choose to visit? And perhaps more importantly: what happens when the next generation grows up thinking autonomous robots moving around a supermarket is completely normal? Will they see Tally as technology? Or simply as part of what a modern store is?
Pickard concluded: “There’s a fascinating intersection here between automation, operations, customer experience and the psychology of physical retail. I’m increasingly convinced that the question isn’t just, what can robots do for retailers? It’s also, what can robots make customers feel about the future of retail?”
White Castle onboard as launch partner as Murphy USA starts roll-out of autonomous hot food platform
Murphy USA, a retailer of gasoline and convenience merchandise with more than 1,800 stores located primarily in the Southwest, Southeast, Midwest and Northeast United States, has announced an initial roll-out of an autonomous foodservice platform in select larger format stores, providing customers another way to access hot, branded food. The platform, developed by Automated Retail Technologies (ART), will launch featuring hamburger chain White Castle.
“We’re continually evaluating opportunities that create additional value for our customers while building on the strengths that have made Murphy USA successful,” says Scott Woodward, Murphy USA Senior Vice President and Chief Merchandising Officer. “This relationship allows us to introduce a new convenience offering informed by customer insights, while maintaining the operational discipline and focus on everyday value. We’re encouraged by the opportunity to drive incremental inside sales, traffic and basket growth.”
“We’ve spent more than a century finding innovative ways to bring our Crave to customers wherever they are,” says Audra Mazzeo, White Castle Vice President of Retail Sales. “This partnership creates a unique opportunity to meet customers during their everyday routines and deliver the White Castle experience in a way that is convenient, fast, and incredibly tasty.”
Customers place orders through a touchscreen interface and receive hot food in approximately two minutes. Behind the scenes, ART’s technology automates preparation, heating, and delivery within a self-contained system. The technology is also designed as a modular, multi-brand platform capable of supporting nationally recognised brands, regional favorites and a variety of food categories over time.
Nathan Davies swaps financial services for retail as he takes on data and AI role at M&S
Nathan Davies has joined Marks & Spencer as Head of Data & AI Delivery.
In a LinkedIn post, Davies, whose CV includes stints at BlackRock and Lloyds Banking Group, said: “M&S is continuing to scale its data and AI ambitions, and my focus will be on building a strong, predictable delivery capability that helps teams turn great ideas into measurable business impact with clarity, pace, quality, and confidence.”
He added: “What I have seen already is the energy, talent, and ambition across the organisation. I look forward to partnering with teams across data technology, product, analytics, governance, operations, and retail to accelerate delivery while maintaining the quality, governance, and operational excellence required for successful scaling.”
“While I am excited about what lies ahead, I am equally grateful to the many people who have supported me on the journey here. To colleagues, leaders, mentors, friends, and family, thank you. Every opportunity is built on the encouragement, trust, and contribution of others. I have always believed that while individual talent matters, it's teams that win. The best outcomes happen when great people come together around a shared purpose, and I look forward to becoming part of that team at M&S. Excited for the journey ahead and ready to get started.”
Japanese fashion retailer UNIQLO lands at Canary Wharf retail and leisure destination in East London
Canary Wharf is getting a new addition to its fashion line-up with the arrival of UNIQLO.
Stuart Fyfe, Managing Director of Retail, Leisure and Hospitality at CWG, says: “We’re absolutely delighted to welcome UNIQLO to Canary Wharf. This is a brand that has built a global following by making exceptional quality feel effortless and accessible. UNIQLO joins a host of innovative, forward thinking brands that are redefining what a world class retail and leisure destination can feel like, and we couldn’t be more excited for them to be part of the story.”
“The momentum we’re seeing across the Wharf this year has been remarkable. Footfall continues to grow, our visitors are spending more time here and the energy across the retail, dining and leisure offer is palpable. UNIQLO aligns with our ambition and amplifies that energy. It’s another clear indication that Canary Wharf is one of London’s most exciting and dynamic destinations.”
UNIQLO follows a number of recent deals including Jigsaw, premium footwear retailer Nokwol, Sushi Dog, Holy Greens making its UK debut, Vagabond, The Tallyman and Bronson Burger. Sea Lanes Canary Wharf - an open air floating swimming pool - opened in June, welcoming more than 30,000 swimmers within the first month of opening.
99% of the estate’s retail and leisure space is currently occupied.
Uber Eats set to launch robot deliveries with Coco Robotics in EU market with Finland up first
Uber Eats is bringing robot delivery to the EU. This week, Finland will become the first EU market where its customers can get their orders delivered by autonomous robots, starting in central Helsinki through a partnership with Coco Robotics. Customers matched with a robot can follow its journey in the Uber Eats app.
A spokesperson says: “We’re growing fast in Finland. We launched Uber Eats in May with three cities, and just three months later we’re adding eight more, bringing us to 11 cities and areas across the country. Helsinki is a particularly exciting place to take this next step: the robots have already been put through their paces on the city’s streets and in Finnish winter conditions. Now they’ll be delivering for Uber Eats alongside our existing courier network.”
Starship Technologies pulls delivery robots from Sheffield streets following vandalism and threats
Starship Technologies has said its fleet of delivery robots will no longer operate in Sheffield. The company launched a pilot in the city in March, with the robots being used to deliver food for Uber Eats.
Ryan Case, Public Affairs and Communication Manager at Starship Technologies, says: “Our pilot in Sheffield has now come to an end, and we have paused the service while we review what we’ve learned. We’ll assess the results of the pilot before deciding on any future deployments of robots in the city. We regularly assess a number of areas across the UK, and Sheffield remains one of them.”
The move comes after a small number of the robots and their infrastructure were vandalised. This included the words ‘off our street’ being daubed across their tops and flags meant for increased visibility being snapped off. Traffic cones were also placed behind robots in an attempt to stop them moving.
Case adds: “There have been a small number of incidents of vandalism in Sheffield, which is disappointing, not least because it affects the local businesses that rely on the robots for deliveries. However, vandalism was not a factor in our decision to pause the service: this was a commercial decision and a natural conclusion to the pilot phase.”
The pilot highlights a key challenge facing autonomous delivery companies. The technology clearly works out in the wild. However, long-term deployments have to win over both customers and communities, whilst proving that the economics work.

items.title: Lord Walker calls for Healey to cut business taxes
items.summary: Iceland boss Lord Richard Walker has urged Andy Burnham and John Healey to cut taxes for businesses and to stop focusing on the cost of living.  Walker, who backed Labour at the last election, said Healey should ease costs for employers. The supermarket chief was the cost of living tsar under Sir Keir Starmer’s government [...]
items.body:
Lord Walker calls for Healey to cut business taxes
Iceland boss Lord Richard Walker has urged Andy Burnham and John Healey to cut taxes for businesses and to stop focusing on the cost of living.
Walker, who backed Labour at the last election, said Healey should ease costs for employers.
The supermarket chief was the cost of living tsar under Sir Keir Starmer’s government before leaving with the change of Prime Minister.
He said on Sunday that “warm words towards business won’t be enough” and added that the government should “stop focusing on the cost of living and start focusing on the cost of getting Britain back to work”.
“Their first priority should be simple: make it cheaper to employ people, invest and grow,” he wrote in The Sun on Sunday.
“Every rise in employers’ National Insurance, every punishing business rates bill, and every other additional cost imposed by Whitehall changes the calculation about whether to create another job.
“The October Budget should begin shifting the tax burden away from jobs and productive investment.”
Tax cut and ending triple lock pension calls
His intervention on Burnham’s cost of living drive is just the latest in a string of attacks on policymaking in the UK.
Before Burnham came into office, he said publicly that Ed Miliband would be a “disaster” as Chancellor as he said energy policy had become “far too ideological”.
In the House of Lords, Walker also hit out at the “unsustainable” triple lock pension, which uprates the state pension every year by whichever is highest out of inflation, wage growth of 2.5 per cent.
Walker echoed the Confederation of British Industry and other business groups’ demands for Burnham to cut national insurance for employers, which was raised by Rachel Reeves in the first budget of the Labour government.
The tax hike in 2024 raised about £25bn yet employers have blamed the added cost of hiring for the dramatic slowdown in the jobs market.
The hospitality sector has meanwhile pushed for Burnham to cut VAT and reform business rates to boost high streets.
Top entrepreneurs and business bosses including John Caudwell and Lord Stuart Rose wrote to the government to “stop the creep” of small tax hikes on businesses and households.
Rose, who is the former chairman of Asda and Marks & Spencer, said he had “never been more concerned about the cost of doing business” and added that taxes and regulation had become “serious impediments to growth and employment”.

items.title: ‘I’ve £80k in the account, here’s my pin’: turning the tables on the scammers
items.summary: Plagued by bank impersonation scams, one Guardian Money reader got even by stringing the fraudsters along … for hours New payment set up? The bank scam where your ‘bank’ is the scammer “A couple of Sundays ago at just past 11am my mobile rang. An automated message purported to be from Barclays Bank, querying a payment to Argos for more than £1,000. Not only had I not made a payment to Argos recently, nor do I bank with Barclays. I am plagued with these kinds of calls. Usually, when possible, I make it clear to the scammers that I know their game. Usually, that call ends there and then. Continue reading...
items.body:
“A couple of Sundays ago at just past 11am my mobile rang. An automated message purported to be from Barclays Bank, querying a payment to Argos for more than £1,000. Not only had I not made a payment to Argos recently, nor do I bank with Barclays.
I am plagued with these kinds of calls. Usually, when possible, I make it clear to the scammers that I know their game. Usually, that call ends there and then.
But this time I realised there was a chance to string them along. It was just a question of how soon they realised I was bluffing. I assumed it would be a couple of minutes. In fact it was three hours.
I called the number shown on my phone and, pretending to be a confused, doddery old man – not that difficult for me – I expressed the expected alarm at the bogus payment.
The man who answered, who had more or less a received pronunciation accent, went through what I understand is the usual story: my credit card had been compromised, bankruptcy was on the horizon, remedial action essential. Someone from the investigations team would call me back, he said. Thirty minutes later someone calling himself “Adam” rang. From here on in the number always came up as “No caller ID”.
Several times Adam ended the call, presumably to consult his fellow crooks, and rang back later.
First, Adam went through several security-like questions. When did I last use my credit card? “Can’t remember,” I replied. What was the last transaction I made? “Dunno.” Did I use internet banking? “No”. Then came the big one: how much is in your current account? “Around £80,000,” I said. (If only.)
There wasn’t a sharp intake of breath. I couldn’t hear a licking of lips. But I could sense that Adam’s vocal cords had tightened, and he was from now on more intense.
He explained it was a matter of the utmost urgency my credit card should be cancelled and a new one issued. Would I like to keep the same pin, he asked? I said “yes” and he asked for it. I’d already written down a made-up pin on a bit of paper, and gave it to him. I thought I could sense him trying hard to remain matter of fact.
He asked if I had my debit card and credit card with me. I said I couldn’t find my credit card. Adam was stern, insisting I look for it. I couldn’t be bothered to fabricate two false 16-digit numbers, and so I told him my wife must have it and she was out. He let this go.
I had already taken out one of my debit cards from my wallet, one issued by HSBC, jotted down the first eight digits and made up eight more. To my surprise, and some alarm, Adam read out the first six digits, correctly, saying the card was issued by HSBC. (How did he know I had an HSBC account?)
He didn’t bother to explain why he needed the debit card, too – or why he needed the numbers – and, being in character I didn’t ask, just went meekly along. I guess the implication was that both cards were compromised and so the investigations team needed to cancel that one as well.
I gave him the made-up number, thinking this would be the end of it. But within a minute he came back and said the number I’d given didn’t seem to be a genuine one.
I assumed concerned bafflement and told him that all I could say was that I was reading out the number on the card in front of me. There was another pause, presumably while he consulted one of his scammer colleagues. To my surprise they decided to keep going.
As this was Sunday, as Adam pointed out, the banks were closed. So the only safe procedure was to send round a courier to pick up my debit card – right now. It couldn’t wait until tomorrow. Was that OK with me? I told him it was fine.
He said I should put the card in an envelope and address it: HSBC Investigations Team, what he thought was my name, Ref HS844677.
He was most insistent on two things: he repeated several times that the courier must, on no account whatsoever, be able to see that a bank card was in the envelope, and that I must seal it extremely carefully.
He insisted three times that I read the address back to him. I pretended to be getting a bit fed up with all this but he explained, quite firmly, that banking security was at stake here and there was no room for error.
A new thought then occurred to him. Did I have a current bank statement, and could I find the most recent one? I noisily opened and shut a drawer. He asked for the balance. I had already written down a precise made-up amount. I told him £81,224.93.
Adam told me he’d ring back when he had booked the courier and got an ETA. He’d already asked me for my postcode and I’d given him one where I lived several years ago. Now he asked for my exact address and I gave him a house number that I knew was too high to exist in that street.
Fifteen minutes later he rang back, sounding a little flustered. A blue Prius was outside the address I’d given but it seemed to be a block of flats. “That’s not right,” I said, “I live in a house.” Another hiatus, as he communicated with the courier. Could I see a blue Prius? he asked. I paused long enough to have looked out of an imaginary window and said “No, I can’t see a blue car”.
What can you see outside your house? he asked. “Nothing,” I said. He rang off again.
Five minutes later he called back. Would I mind going out and trying to find the blue Prius? I explained that I had a bad leg and couldn’t leave my house at all. But I would gladly open the front door and have a look. Then another call. The driver was absolutely adamant that the address was in a block of flats.
I’d kept this charade up for a lot longer than I’d expected and I was about to go out. “Oh dear,” I said in my best whispery voice, “it looks like I’ve been wasting your time.”
What? I switched into my own voice to deliver the – unprintable – coup de grace, and hang up.
Adam even had the cheek to ring back later. I didn’t answer. I wish I had. I could have thanked him for the afternoon’s entertainment.

LOOKFANTASTIC is evolving its Beauty Pro Programme as the LF Network of Experts, reinforcing its long-standing commitment to supporting beauty talent by connecting established beauty expertise and the trusted voices shaping the industry today. The Network brings together over 3,000 dermatologists, aestheticians, makeup artists, hairstylists, editors, writers and creators, alongside other established and emerging voices […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! items.body:
LOOKFANTASTIC is evolving its Beauty Pro Programme as the LF Network of Experts, reinforcing its long-standing commitment to supporting beauty talent by connecting established beauty expertise and the trusted voices shaping the industry today.
The Network brings together over 3,000 dermatologists, aestheticians, makeup artists, hairstylists, editors, writers and creators, alongside other established and emerging voices with the knowledge, experience and perspective to influence how beauty is understood, discovered and experienced.
LF Network of Experts sits at the intersection of professional expertise, creator-led education, brand partnership and commerce, creating a bridge between the people with specialist knowledge and the communities looking to them for guidance. By bringing together established industry professionals, emerging creators and trusted beauty voices, LOOKFANTASTIC is creating an ecosystem where expertise can be shared, amplified and translated into opportunity. The Network gives experts new ways
to turn what they know and the influence they have built into meaningful career opportunities.
Members of the Network will have access to opportunities spanning affiliate partnerships and codes, masterclasses, social and content training, event hosting and connections with leading beauty brands. Whether helping an expert earn from the recommendations their community trusts, develop their craft, build their profile or create new industry connections, the programme is designed to support beauty talent at every stage of their journey.
Keely Gough, LOOKFANTASTIC managing director, said: LF Experts is rooted in the belief that credible, practical expertise has never been more valuable in beauty and we know beauty discovery has moved beyond the salon and treatment room, with communities forming across social and digital platforms and a new generation of trusted voices emerging alongside traditional industry authorities.
Expert recommendations, peer reviews, social content and educational platforms have all become an important part of how consumers navigate the beauty landscape and as consumers face more products, content and opinions than ever before, trusted guidance has never been more valuable. We’re excited to champion the people behind that expertise and support opportunities to develop their careers, grow their profiles and turn their knowledge and influence into new possibilities.
LOOKFANTASTIC’s connection to professional beauty expertise dates back to its roots in salons and hairdressing education. In 2020, as the COVID-19 pandemic brought unprecedented disruption to the beauty industry, this heritage evolved into the Beauty Pro community. The Beauty Pro community was created to support professionals at a time when salons, clinics and beauty businesses were forced to close their doors. But as the industry emerged from the pandemic, the way consumers experienced, discovered and shopped beauty had changed too. LF Network of Experts has been created in response to this evolution, bringing together a wider generation of voices leading the conversation and shaping the future of beauty.
The Network will continue to evolve alongside the people it represents. LF Experts will listen to member feedback and use those insights to shape future opportunities, ensuring the programme remains relevant to the changing needs of beauty professionals and the wider industry.
From its origins supporting professionals through one of the most challenging periods the beauty industry has faced, to its new role championing the diverse voices defining beauty today, LF Network of Experts marks the next chapter in LOOKFANTASTIC’s commitment to beauty expertise.

items.body:
Oak Furnitureland, the specialist furniture and homewares retailer, has announced plans to open a new showroom in Ipswich this weekend on Saturday 29th August, bringing its collection of stylish, high-quality furniture to even more customers across the country.
Located at Euro Park Retail Park, the 17,000 sq. ft showroom will showcase the retailer’s expanding ‘Whole Home’ proposition, featuring a series of fully styled room sets to help customers visualise looks across living, dining, and bedroom spaces.
The offering will include several new ranges including the Savannah and Corton collections which feature elevated and modern cabinetry designed for the living room, bedroom, and dining spaces such as TV units, coffee tables, and bedframes.
Customers will also be able to try the new Phoenix CineLuxe and Hadley sofas. A high-back recliner, the Hadley is also complete with a USB-C charging port while the Phoenix tech sofa features reclining seats and integrated speakers for a fully immersive experience – perfect for film fans.
The opening has created seven new jobs locally, including roles across sales and showroom management.
Lee Finch, Showroom Manager, said: “The team is really excited to open the doors to our new Ipswich showroom this weekend. We’re looking forward to welcoming customers from the local area and beyond to our store, and our team will be on hand to help you choose the right pieces for your home.”
Alex Fisher, chief executive of Oak Furnitureland, said: “It’s great to be opening a new showroom in Ipswich – it’s an important step as we continue to invest in our network across the UK. We’re really proud of our expanding range of high-quality, stylish furniture – offering great value at outstanding prices, and which is designed to grow with our customers’ homes. We’re looking forward to welcoming people from across Suffolk to the new store soon.”
Last year, the retailer launched its Lifetime Furniture Guarantee, which covers the structural framework of both cabinet and upholstery collections and demonstrates a clear commitment to furniture built to last. Flexible interest-free credit options are also available, making stylish, high-quality furniture for the whole home accessible to even more homes and families
This latest opening takes their estate to 70 showrooms nationwide, as Oak Furnitureland continues to invest in its retail estate while enhancing the experience for customers both in-showroom and online.

items.body:
Aldi has revealed the next 25 locations to benefit from its £300 million investment in upgrading existing stores across the UK this year.
Stores in London, Liverpool, Aberdeen, Sunderland and Bedford are among those receiving refurbishments and other improvements, including more energy-efficient technology.
Five stores – in Stirling, Paisley, Wollaston, Linlithgow and Lewes – will also be extended as part of the investment programme.
Changes will vary by store, with selected locations benefiting from upgrades to Bakery, Health & Beauty and fresh food areas.
The programme will also introduce more sustainable features, including energy-efficient fridge doors and natural refrigerants designed to help reduce carbon emissions.
Jonathan Neale, Managing Director of National Real Estate at Aldi UK, said: “We’re continuing to invest in our existing stores because we know how important the in-store experience is to customers.
“These upgrades will create more space, improve key areas of our stores and make them easier to shop. It’s an important part of how we’re investing in the communities we serve.”
The 25 Aldi locations receiving upgrades are:
- Arndale, Manchester

items.body:
ITVET, one of the UK’s leading technology partners for the retail and commercial property industry, appointed Toolbox Marketing earlier this year as its strategic marketing agency to support the next stage of its growth.
The partnership brings together more than 45 years of combined industry experience, uniting ITVET’s proven technical expertise with Toolbox Marketing’s specialist marketing knowledge in the commercial real estate sector.
Over the years, ITVET has built an exceptional reputation through delivering outstanding service, technical excellence and long-term client relationships. Growing to a team of more than 100 colleagues, the business has achieved its success almost entirely through referrals and word-of-mouth recommendations.
Now, as the business continues to evolve, ITVET has chosen to invest in a strategic marketing partner to better communicate its expertise, strengthen its brand presence and share the stories behind the people and projects that have made it a trusted name across the sector.
Tommy Pell, Director at ITVET, said: “We’ve never been a business that shouts about what we do. Our focus has always been on delivering exceptional service for our clients, and that’s been the foundation of our growth. Thanks to our incredible team, we’ve built a business of more than 500 clients almost entirely through reputation and recommendation.”
“As we look to the future, we felt the time was right to work with a partner who truly understands our industry and can help us tell our story without changing who we are. Toolbox Marketing shares our values, understands the markets we operate in, and will help us showcase the expertise that has always existed behind the scenes.”
Toolbox Marketing will provide strategic marketing insight and brand consultancy, helping ITVET increase its visibility while remaining true to the culture, customer focus, and work ethic that have underpinned the company’s success.
Ben Hammond, growth manager at Toolbox Marketing, added: “As soon as we started talking with ITVET, I knew there was a fantastic story waiting to be told. Our job is to make sure the market sees the same expertise and passion that ITVET’s clients have experienced for years.”
The appointment marks the beginning of a long-term partnership focused on strengthening ITVET’s market presence while supporting the company’s continued growth across the UK.

items.title: Three top tips for keeping online gaming fun and safe
items.summary: Discover what's happening in retail today, Retail Times publishes international & UK retail news covering products, data, tech, packaging, people, research, comment and much more. Online games are meant to be an easy way to unwind, yet they don’t always feel that simple. You might sit down for a quick session and suddenly realise more time has passed than you expected, or you’ve spent more money than you meant to. That slight loss of control can take the shine off […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! Retail Times - Retail Times, a free to view retail news website
items.body:
Online games are meant to be an easy way to unwind, yet they don’t always feel that simple. You might sit down for a quick session and suddenly realise more time has passed than you expected, or you’ve spent more money than you meant to. That slight loss of control can take the shine off what should feel fun and relaxing.
Fortunately, you don’t need to overhaul how you play to fix this. A few small, practical habits can help you stay in charge, so your gaming time feels calm, enjoyable and fully on your terms.
- Set a personal entertainment budget
It helps to decide what you’re comfortable with before you start playing. This step gives you a clear boundary, so you don’t have to think about spending in the moment. For example, you might set aside the same amount you’d usually spend on a takeaway coffee or a streaming subscription.
Planning your budget for everyday costs can help you figure out a simple weekly boundary. This approach keeps gaming in its place as entertainment, not something that competes with bills or essentials. You stay relaxed because you already know where you stand.
- Use promotions wisely (don’t chase them)
Offers can add a bit of excitement, especially when they include free-entry games or small prizes. You’ll often see bingo promotions on leading platforms, and they can be a nice bonus when they match how you already play.
However, it’s easy to get caught up in trying to keep up with every new offer. Instead, focus on the ones that genuinely suit your routine. For example, if you usually play for 20 minutes in the evening, choose promotions that fit into that window rather than stretching your time.
This habit helps you stay in control and keeps the experience feeling light rather than pressured.
- Make the most of in-built controls
Most devices now include simple tools that help you manage your screen time without much effort. Features like Digital Wellbeing on Android phones let you set daily limits or reminders, so you don’t lose track of time.
You might, for instance, set a gentle alert after 30 minutes. This reminder doesn’t interrupt your fun, but it gives you a moment to check in with yourself.
Likewise, app timers can pause access once you reach your limit, making it easier to stick to the boundaries you set earlier. These small controls support your routine without adding extra hassle.
Final thoughts…
When you keep gaming simple, it tends to stay enjoyable. These suggestions work together to support that feeling. Instead of overthinking it, aim to create a space where you can dip in and out, enjoy a bit of entertainment and then move on with your day.
When you feel in control of your time and your spending, online gaming remains an easy, enjoyable way to unwind on your terms – exactly what it should be.

items.title: Labour can boost growth at Budget says Asda boss - but it must change tack and ditch heavy high street taxes
items.summary: Allan Leighton also threw his support behind Mike Ashley's scathing remarks on Burnham's plans to revive the high street.
items.body:
Labour can boost growth at Budget says Asda boss - but it must change tack and ditch heavy high street taxes
- See more This is Money on Google - save us as a Preferred Source
The boss of Asda has warned of a Budget 'tipping point' as Labour has the chance to boost growth instead of squeezing business with even more tax hikes
Allan Leighton also threw his support behind Mike Ashley's scathing remarks on Andy Burnham's plans to revive the high street and urged him against heaping more taxes on larger retailers.
The chairman's comments come as business leaders have started to set out their case to ministers ahead of the October Budget and as he revealed signs of a turnaround at Britain's third biggest grocer.
He said the Budget was an opportunity for the new Prime Minister and Chancellor to shift away from a model of heavy taxes on business which inhibits growth to one that enhances it.
'This is a real tipping point: instead of just talking about growth, the government now has an opportunity to change tack and actually make growth happen.'
Asda boss Allan Leighton has said the Budget will be a 'tipping point' that could set the scene for future economic growth - or result in large firms finding it harder to invest
Leighton added that the next couple of months were 'critical' as consumers' confidence when they return from their summer holidays will 'set the scene for the rest for the year,' including the important Christmas trading period.
It comes as Sports Direct Tycoon Mike Ashley this week said that it would be 'disastrous' to tax larger retailers more in order to fund discounts for other businesses like pubs.
Burnham this week insisted he would 'take pressure off' businesses, which have complained about consumers having less cash to spend while their own operating costs have soared in recent years.
His plans include funding business rates discounts for pubs and clubs by increasing business rates on online retail warehouses as well as tougher rules for vape and betting shops.
Mike Ashley - whose stable of retailers encompasses House of Fraser, Flannels, Sofa.com, Jack Wills and Evans Cycles - said that it would be 'simply delusional' to tax larger retailers more through raising rates further.
He lambasted a 'disastrous' approach to business rates and 'the dramatically increasing cost of employing people' as the biggest obstacles for businesses.
Leighton said that Ashley's comments were 'absolutely right'.
He added: 'All of the things that have been the policy so far have added cost to, not just retail, across the piece. And then that has reduced the profitability of those organisations, and therefore they've got less money to invest in growth. It's economics 101.'
It comes as Leighton hailed signs of a revival at Asda, which has been struggling with falling sales since its takeover by a private equity firm a few years ago.
Sales rose 0.2pc over the seven weeks to 18 August, in a return to growth for the first time in more than two years. Leighton called this 'an important milestone'.
He said the group was 'about a third' of the way through its recovery, which has included slashing prices and a major online upgrade.
But Asda said sales fell 2.3pc for the three months to the end of June, with revenue of £5.1bn.
'I see this really as the sort of foothills of recovery still, but also the foothills of possibility,' Leighton added.
Earlier this year, Asda accounts revealed that pre-tax losses had widened from £599million in 2024 to £989million in 2025, as total sales fell 3.4 per cent to £25.9billion.
Leighton, who rejoined the Leeds-based retailer in November 2024, has warned that his revival plan will not be an overnight fix and slashing prices will hit profits.
But he warned there was pressure on prices due to the heatwave impacting crops this summer.
'The crops are in a tricky state, not just in the UK, everywhere, you know clearly and it's more a produce issue than anything else.'
He said that the grocer had thousands of producers and growers and is 'working very hard with them' to ensure availability 'sticks up as well as we can' and to 'manage the inflation in the best way we can.'
'We generally inflate below the market anyway, so generally when there's high inflation, that's quite a good thing for us.'
He added: 'But the biggest thing is consumer sentiment. How do people feel? Do they feel as if they want to spend? Do they have the money to spend? That's always been the driver of it.'

items.body:
John Iles, 46, of no fixed abode, was sentenced to 82 weeks in prison at Bristol Magistrates’ Court.
Iles was charged with nine counts of shop theft and one count of parcel theft.
He targeted several retailers, including supermarkets and convenience stores, in Bradley Stoke, Downend and Staple Hill.
He also stole hundreds of pounds worth of steaks from Aldi and Tesco and has been ordered to pay compensation of varying amounts to the businesses he targeted.
PC James Mullin, officer in the case, said: “We welcome the custodial sentence which has been handed to Iles, who is a prolific shoplifter who shows a total disregard for his actions.
“Shoplifting is not a victimless crime and the harm it can cause businesses and the wider community is immeasurable.
“Not only does the loss of merchandise effect the running of a business, but the theft and related anti-social behaviour can cause harassment, alarm and distress to shop owners and staff.”
